/-!
# Serre's positivity conjecture

Let $R$ be a (Noetherian) commutative regular local ring and let $P, Q$ be prime ideals of $R$
such that $R/P \otimes_R R/Q$ has finite length. Serre defined the intersection multiplicity of
$R/P$ and $R/Q$ by
$$\chi(R/P, R/Q) := \sum_{i \ge 0} (-1)^i \ell_R(\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(R/P, R/Q)),$$
where $\ell_R$ denotes the length of an $R$-module. The sum is finite because a regular local ring
has finite global dimension.

Serre's *positivity conjecture* states that if $\dim(R/P) + \dim(R/Q) = \dim(R)$ then
$\chi(R/P, R/Q) > 0$. It is the last of Serre's four multiplicity conjectures that remains open
in general.

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Serre's multiplicity
  conjectures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serre%27s_multiplicity_conjectures)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in
  mathematics](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/List_of_unsolved_problems_in_mathematics#Algebra)
- J.-P. Serre, *Local Algebra*, Springer Monographs in Mathematics, 2000.
-/

blocks.docstring:
A commutative ring $R$ is a *regular local ring* if it is a Noetherian local ring whose Krull
dimension equals the dimension of its cotangent space $\mathfrak{m} / \mathfrak{m}^2$ over the
residue field $R / \mathfrak{m}$ (equivalently, by Nakayama's lemma, the maximal ideal
$\mathfrak{m}$ can be generated by $\dim R$ elements).

noncomputable def intersectionMultiplicity (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ i : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ i *
    (Module.length R
      (((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj (ModuleCat.of R M)).obj (ModuleCat.of R N))).toNat
blocks.docstring:
**Serre's intersection multiplicity** of two modules $M$ and $N$ over a commutative ring $R$:
$$\chi(M, N) := \sum_{i \ge 0} (-1)^i \ell_R(\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M, N)),$$
where $\ell_R$ denotes the length of an $R$-module.

This is meaningful when every $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M, N)$ has finite length and only finitely
many of them are nonzero, e.g. when $R$ is a regular local ring (which has finite global
dimension), $M$ and $N$ are finitely generated and $M \otimes_R N$ has finite length. Outside of
this situation the value is a junk value: an infinite length is counted as $0$ (via `ENat.toNat`),
and a sum with infinitely many nonzero terms is $0$ (via `finsum`).

justification.closest_existing_considered: CategoryTheory.Tor / Tor' (Mathlib/CategoryTheory/Monoidal/Tor.lean) and Module.length (Mathlib/RingTheory/Length.lean), which are used as the building blocks; no Euler-characteristic-of-Tor definition exists in Mathlib or FormalConjecturesForMathlib.

claims.decomposer_note: Single open universal claim (Serre's positivity conjecture); the statement omits Serre's standing hypothesis ℓ_R(R/P ⊗_R R/Q) = ℓ_R(R/(P+Q)) < ∞ (P+Q primary to the maximal ideal), which must be added for χ(R/P,R/Q) := Σ_i (-1)^i ℓ_R(Tor_i^R(R/P,R/Q)) to be defined (the sum is finite since R is regular local, hence Noetherian of finite global dimension), and dim denotes Krull dimension; the solved companion conjectures (dimension inequality, non-negativity, vanishing) and the known special cases (Dutta 2008, Skalit 2019) in the article are not posed by the statement and are not included.
claims.reviewer_why: All eight candidates compile and encode the same faithful mathematics (regular local ring := Noetherian local with embedding dim = Krull dim, or equivalently μ(𝔪) = dim R; χ := alternating sum of Module.length of CategoryTheory.Tor (ModuleCat R) objects; dim := ringKrullDim; Serre's standing hypothesis ℓ(R/P ⊗ R/Q) < ∞ added as required by the decomposition notes; strict conclusion 0 < χ in ℤ). c01 is the most polished: a Prop-class IsRegularLocalRing extending IsLocalRing/IsNoetherianRing with field and DVR test instances, a general intersectionMultiplicity with a test lemma, the finite-length hypothesis stated literally as in the article, and docstrings that record the unreachable junk-value conventions. Alternatives were weaker in style only: c03/c08 truncate the sum at an ad hoc bound (embedding dim / Krull dim), c04 places the implication after the colon, c05 uses tsum, c08 quantifies ∀ R inside the statement with only AMS 13. The file was shipped unchanged; it compiles with only the sorry warning.

In mathematics, Serre's multiplicity conjectures, named after Jean-Pierre Serre, are certain problems in commutative algebra, motivated by the needs of algebraic geometry. Since André Weil's initial definition of intersection numbers, around 1949, there had been a question of how to provide a more flexible and computable theory, which Serre sought to address. In 1958, Serre realized the classical algebraic-geometric ideas of multiplicity could be generalized using the concepts of homological algebra.

import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!

$$\chi(R/P, R/Q) := \sum_{i \ge 0} (-1)^i \ell_R(\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(R/P, R/Q)),$$

Serre's *positivity conjecture* states that if $\dim(R/P) + \dim(R/Q) = \dim(R)$ then
$\chi(R/P, R/Q) > 0$. It is the last of Serre's four multiplicity conjectures that remains open

*References:*
- [Wikipedia, Serre's multiplicity
  conjectures](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Serre%27s_multiplicity_conjectures)
- [Wikipedia, List of unsolved problems in

- J.-P. Serre, *Local Algebra*, Springer Monographs in Mathematics, 2000.

namespace SerresPositivityConjecture

universe u

open CategoryTheory IsLocalRing

open scoped TensorProduct

/-- A commutative ring $R$ is a *regular local ring* if it is a Noetherian local ring whose Krull
dimension equals the dimension of its cotangent space $\mathfrak{m} / \mathfrak{m}^2$ over the
residue field $R / \mathfrak{m}$ (equivalently, by Nakayama's lemma, the maximal ideal
$\mathfrak{m}$ can be generated by $\dim R$ elements). -/
class IsRegularLocalRing (R : Type*) [CommRing R] : Prop
    extends IsLocalRing R, IsNoetherianRing R where
  finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_ringKrullDim :
    Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) = ringKrullDim R

/-- A field is a regular local ring (of dimension $0$). -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
instance (K : Type*) [Field K] : IsRegularLocalRing K where
  finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_ringKrullDim := by
    rw [finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_zero, ringKrullDim_eq_zero_of_field, Nat.cast_zero]

/-- A discrete valuation ring is a regular local ring (of dimension $1$). -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
instance (R : Type*) [CommRing R] [IsDomain R] [IsDiscreteValuationRing R] :
    IsRegularLocalRing R where
  finrank_cotangentSpace_eq_ringKrullDim := by
    rw [finrank_CotangentSpace_eq_one,
      IsPrincipalIdealRing.ringKrullDim_eq_one R (IsDiscreteValuationRing.not_isField R),
      Nat.cast_one]

variable (R : Type u) [CommRing R]

/-- **Serre's intersection multiplicity** of two modules $M$ and $N$ over a commutative ring $R$:
$$\chi(M, N) := \sum_{i \ge 0} (-1)^i \ell_R(\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M, N)),$$
where $\ell_R$ denotes the length of an $R$-module.

This is meaningful when every $\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(M, N)$ has finite length and only finitely
many of them are nonzero, e.g. when $R$ is a regular local ring (which has finite global
dimension), $M$ and $N$ are finitely generated and $M \otimes_R N$ has finite length. Outside of
this situation the value is a junk value: an infinite length is counted as $0$ (via `ENat.toNat`),
and a sum with infinitely many nonzero terms is $0$ (via `finsum`). -/
noncomputable def intersectionMultiplicity (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M] [Module R M]
    [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] : ℤ :=
  ∑ᶠ i : ℕ, (-1 : ℤ) ^ i *
    (Module.length R
      (((Tor (ModuleCat.{u} R) i).obj (ModuleCat.of R M)).obj (ModuleCat.of R N))).toNat

/-- Over the trivial ring every module has length $0$, so all intersection multiplicities
vanish. -/
@[category test, AMS 13]
theorem intersectionMultiplicity_of_subsingleton [Subsingleton R] (M N : Type u) [AddCommGroup M]
    [Module R M] [AddCommGroup N] [Module R N] : intersectionMultiplicity R M N = 0 := by
  simp [intersectionMultiplicity]

/-- **Serre's positivity conjecture**

Let $R$ be a commutative regular local ring and let $P, Q$ be prime ideals of $R$ such that
$\ell_R(R/P \otimes_R R/Q) < \infty$ (Serre's standing hypothesis, needed for
$\chi(R/P, R/Q) = \sum_{i \ge 0} (-1)^i \ell_R(\operatorname{Tor}_i^R(R/P, R/Q))$ to be defined).
If $\dim(R/P) + \dim(R/Q) = \dim(R)$, then $\chi(R/P, R/Q) > 0$. -/
@[category research open, AMS 13 14]
theorem serres_positivity_conjecture [IsRegularLocalRing R] (P Q : Ideal R) [P.IsPrime] [Q.IsPrime]
    (hfin : Module.length R ((R ⧸ P) ⊗[R] (R ⧸ Q)) < ⊤)
    (hdim : ringKrullDim (R ⧸ P) + ringKrullDim (R ⧸ Q) = ringKrullDim R) :
    0 < intersectionMultiplicity R (R ⧸ P) (R ⧸ Q) := by
  sorry

end SerresPositivityConjecture

items: Regular local ring is defined as a Noetherian local ring with Module.finrank (ResidueField R) (CotangentSpace R) = ringKrullDim R (embedding dimension = Krull dimension). This is the standard textbook definition; the equivalent 'maximal ideal generated by dim R elements' (via Ideal.spanFinrank) was not used. Two test instances (fields, DVRs) check it.

Serre's standing hypothesis ℓ_R(R/P ⊗_R R/Q) < ∞, which the list entry omits but the article and the decomposition notes require, is added literally as `Module.length R ((R ⧸ P) ⊗[R] (R ⧸ Q)) < ⊤` (rather than the equivalent ℓ_R(R/(P+Q)) < ∞). Without it the statement is false (e.g. P = Q = (x) in k[[x,y]] satisfies the dimension equation).

Tor_i^R(M,N) is taken as `((CategoryTheory.Tor (ModuleCat R) i).obj (ModuleCat.of R M)).obj (ModuleCat.of R N)`, i.e. the left derived functor of M ⊗ - evaluated at N (Mathlib's `Tor`, not `Tor'`); Tor is balanced so this agrees with any other standard definition up to isomorphism, hence has the same length.

χ is defined as `∑ᶠ i : ℕ, (-1)^i * (Module.length R (Tor_i)).toNat : ℤ`. `finsum` returns 0 for infinite support and `ENat.toNat ⊤ = 0`; both defaults are unreachable under the theorem's hypotheses (regular local ⇒ finite global dimension so only finitely many Tor_i are nonzero; ℓ(R/P ⊗ R/Q) < ∞ ⇒ every Tor_i, being f.g. and killed by P+Q, has finite length), so the value equals Serre's χ. The docstring records this.

dim denotes Krull dimension: `ringKrullDim (R ⧸ P)`, `ringKrullDim R` in WithBot ℕ∞; for a Noetherian local ring and its nontrivial quotients these are honest finite naturals so the WithBot ℕ∞ addition in `hdim` is the ordinary sum.
Modules M, N in `intersectionMultiplicity` are required to live in the same universe as R because Mathlib's monoidal structure on `ModuleCat.{u} R` needs this; R ⧸ P and R ⧸ Q automatically do.

Primality of P and Q is given as instance arguments `[P.IsPrime] [Q.IsPrime]` (Mathlib's IsPrime includes P ≠ ⊤). The 'Noetherian' qualifier of the article is part of the definition of regular local ring, as usual.
AMS tags 13 (commutative algebra) and 14 (algebraic geometry) were chosen for the main statement.

references.title: Positivity of intersection multiplicity over a two-dimensional base

reviewer_notes: The list-entry statement omits Serre's standing hypothesis ℓ_R(R/P ⊗_R R/Q) < ∞; without it the claim is false (e.g. P = Q = (x) in k[[x,y]] satisfies the dimension equation) and χ is undefined, so it was added as `Module.length R ((R ⧸ P) ⊗[R] (R ⧸ Q)) < ⊤`, matching the article. Mathlib (this checkout) has no regular local ring predicate and no Serre intersection multiplicity, so both are bespoke, kept in the problem file. Junk-value conventions (finsum over infinite support = 0, ENat.toNat ⊤ = 0) are unreachable under the theorem's hypotheses: a regular local ring has finite global dimension (Auslander–Buchsbaum–Serre) and each Tor_i(R/P,R/Q) is finitely generated and annihilated by the 𝔪-primary ideal P+Q, hence of finite length. The elaborated terms were inspected with pp.explicit: Module.length uses the R-module structure of the ModuleCat Tor object and regularity is ↑(finrank_k(𝔪/𝔪²)) = ringKrullDim R in WithBot ℕ∞. Hypotheses are satisfiable (k[[x,y]], P=(x), Q=(y)); the boundary case R a field, P = Q = 𝔪 gives χ = 1 > 0, consistent with the statement. No candidate omitted the slot and no objections to the decomposition were raised.

title: Serre's positivity conjecture
